subject: maths
question: A moneylender borrows money at 4% per annum and pays the interest at the end of the year. He lends it at 8% per annum compound interest, compounded half-yearly, and receives the interest at the end of the year. In this way, he gains ₹166.4 a year. Find the amount of money he borrows.
solution:
**Given:**

Borrowing Rate = 4% per annum.

Lending Rate = 8% per annum compounded half-yearly.

Gain = ₹166.4 per year.

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Formula for half-yearly = A = P (1 + (r)/(2 times 100))²t 

Simple Interest Formula = SI = (P times r times t)/(100)

**Calculation:**

Let the amount of money borrowed be ₹P.

Interest paid at the end of the year = (P times 4 times 1)/(100) = 0.04P

Interest received at the end of the year (compounded half-yearly) = P (1 + (8)/(2 times 100))² - P

Interest received = P (1 + 0.04)² - P

Interest received = P (1.04²) - P 

Interest received = P (1.0816) - P

Interest received = 1.0816P - P

Interest received = 0.0816P

Gain = Interest received - Interest paid

₹166.4 = 0.0816P - 0.04P

₹166.4 = 0.0416P

⇒ P = (166.4)/(0.0416)

⇒ P = 4000

**The amount of money he borrows is ₹4,000.**
